steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* Never imagined we'd get a hot meal indoors safe and sound, after so many days on the run.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: That Bagpipe girl must be the darling of everyone. We were all gushing to her about how good her stew was.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Mm, she's definitely not bad on that front.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: How's your discussion on settling down? Has it been smooth?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We're all decided. Anyone who can't handle rushing'll stay behind. They'll borrow two storehouses to tuck away in for the next two days.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Refugees scuffling with caravans but never actually stealing anything, that's dead common. The law won't get hung up on that.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: In a few days, they won't be mentioning it on the radio anymore, and we won't need to hide. Then we can get to building our own houses.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er, but the few with Oripathy'll be living a bit ways out from the village.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: The people here are very friendly.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* Yeah, they are. If anyone sheltered us while we were still running, we wouldn't be in this sty of a state now.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Not that it's anyone's fault. Didn't used to be much hassle taking in a bunch of refugees or the like, but life's getting scarier for everyone now.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Look at Selmon, the colleen. If she and her brother had someplace to take them in, she wouldn't be running from settlement to settlement, kicking up all this fuss.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: She could spend the night in the village like us, but she's all stubborn about hiding outside. Since she stole a man's stockbeast here once, see, and now she's awkward about running into him...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...*sigh* You never heard it from me. You let her know, she'll be on my case about disrespecting her again.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Good evening...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Oh, Moran? What are you doing here, so dark out? I'll send you back while the lamps are still lit...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Thank you, but I'm used to making my way in the dark by now...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Is Reed here, if you don't mind?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You're looking for her? She went out on her own.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Maybe Reed's got something on her mind... Selmon hasn't spoken so much as a word to her since she got here.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Don't worry, Bagpipe's gone to find her.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Hm... actually, put it this way. Our bigger concern is if Reed gets annoyed by the noise.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Whoa, sorry!

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...It's alright.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, I wasn't watchin' out, didn't think there'd be anyone here. It all goes pitch dark every time they sound the bell. Takes a moment for my eyes to adjust.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Lucky it's you I ran into. Might've knocked anyone else clean over.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Thought they said they wouldn't need anyone on watch tonight, though?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I just... wanted to sit for a while outside.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, it's the smell of the hay, isn't it? Wonderful, that.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Hay?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Yeah, that's hay piles over there. Been ages since I was around the smell, so I came out to get a proper whiff of them.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Back when I was preppin' to get into military school, I'd have headaches from studyin' so much theory. So I'd just get onto a hay pile and lie back for a bit, and I'd feel right as rain again.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Mum always told me off for bein' lazy, said I shouldn't quit thinkin' about questions just because thinkin' gets too hard... but havin' too much stuff goin' on in your brain does wear a person out, y'know.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: So, give me your hand a sec?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Come on, here now, let's lie down together! Just for a bit!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'm not so good at thinkin' over stuff, so I might not be of much help to you, but the hay will be, I'm sure of it!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Hup—!
Bagpipe relaxes and lies back on the hay pile, lightly humming a folksong she learned just a while ago from the farmers.
A gentle night breeze passes by. Reed follows her suggestion, and takes a deep breath.
But what she smells isn't the aroma of hay—it is, instead, damp mud and ash.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: When it hits me how I've spent three years without goin' home, it always feels so funny.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Think about it. The ground's waitin' for you to till it, the wheat's waitin' for you to reap it... Spend one year away, and you miss an entire go round of all the important stuff, every bit of it.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I can't even get my letters from home until the next time I'm back on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Do you... miss home very much?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Course I do. You? Were you from County Hillock?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But I used to live in a city about the same as County Hillock... flushed red bricks, grey pavements. Buildings two or three floors high, flowering vines growing around the windows.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I... yearn after those peaceful times a lot.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There were so many old books at home, and some manuscripts too. I liked to hide away in the study, and lock the door, so I wouldn't have to hear anyone talk to me.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, you had piles of family makin' a racket, then? Or was it visitors all the time?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...No, thankfully. Just—I could avoid so much trouble if I hid.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I could see into the street from the window in there. I'd see my parents come back after a day of work.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I would love to go back there, if I could.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh. So the place isn't...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'm sorry... I'm makin' it worse for you, aren't I?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's okay. It was all so long ago.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I might not be much different—to the ordinary people whose lives were ruined at County Hillock, or to these refugees leaving their home behind.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They can all settle down here, and rebuild their houses... but—where is their homeland?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: And the ones who are—forced out even farther... where are they fleeing to?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Hmm... You're havin' trouble answerin' these questions just on your lonesome, aren't you?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But I'm not sayin' it's no use thinkin' over them!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: If you can't come up with an answer alone, we can think together. Whenever I had a question I couldn't fill in, I'd always bother Chenchen about it.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: And later down the line, I'd prattle on at my captains... I mean, they found me annoyin' as flip, but still, they'd chat with me every time, help me solve issues.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: What about you? You got anyone to speak your mind to? Like a sister or a schoolmate or someone in arms, that sort of...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There's... my older sister.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You don't get along much?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...No. I shouldn't be saying this. I shouldn't...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Y'know, Selmon was right about one thing, actually. You're always sayin' 'no' out of habit.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But she misunderstood a little. It's when you're talkin' about yourself that you're most fond of sayin' 'no', like... och, I can't put it into words. It's like you're strainin' to break away from somethin'.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...I've been told something like that before.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, what? Really?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: She... saved me, and told me, I didn't have to seek death. That I could dodge destiny.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Outcast, eh. There's somethin' she would say.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I regret... I regret not having it in me to say anything more to her.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I want to ask her so badly—why save me?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: What... did she see in me?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ohh. I'm not sure how she'd answer myself.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But, y'know, Reed, why not ask yourself before askin' her? What do you see in yourself?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: My... self?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, someone's over there.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: With the way they feel about, I think it's Moran... She can't see at night.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Gosh, why's she out here by herself, then?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Miss Moran! Need any help from us?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, you just stand still there for a sec, we'll be right over.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Where's Reed, can I ask? They said, she'd gone out.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm right here.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Sorry. Excuse me, but am I able to go with you?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I don't mind where it is. I've still got some strength, I can work... and fight.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You want to... fight?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I do. They all say I won't live much longer, that my only option's dying without a word in some corner.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I don't agree with that.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: 'If you want to survive as a Taran, then change workshops, and accept lower pay'. 'If you want to survive as with Oripathy, then move out, and get to the Infected neighborhood'...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I'm done listening to all that.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Reed, I used to not be this way, but then I met you.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: They tell me you're an Infected too. It's you who convinced Selmon and the rest to bring us here.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You... trust me, like Fionn does?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Please, no pressure, I... I don't want to be a burden on you, or anyone.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I just want to do something, anything. People like me have nothing left to lose as is.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: If I can bring something or other to the rest of the Tarans, then I want to do it. If my legs will still walk forward, then I want to go with you.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I think that's fine. Reed, for now, let's go together. How about it?
To the red-haired Vouivre, the question's not one Reed needs to respond to, because she starts pulling Reed along before an answer even comes.
Reed takes a glance back at their visitor. She knows Moran has night blindness, and needs someone to guide the way when darkness falls.
With little time to hesitate, Reed extends a hand to Moran.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Let's go.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: Here you finally are, Miss Harmonie. I was beginning to think I'd never see you today.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: A wine tasting courtesy of the Viscount? How could I ever miss it?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: But of course, but of course. A friend of the Marquess of Trent! You're the Viscount's guest of honor.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: It's all thanks to your introducing me that I closed out that bit of prior business. I've been looking for an opportunity to thank you all this time.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Oh, it was quite nothing, Mr. Hall.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: I've no noble personage, or even property in my name. At most, I'm just a messenger, scampering around so the ones in charge don't have to.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: (Toasts)

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Who might he be...?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: The council's pet. A Mr. Fischer.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Oh? Well, I've certainly never heard of him before.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: He only transferred to this county a short while ago. Youngsters like him tend to have to break their backs a little if they want a quick promotion.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Heheh. A universal truth, no?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: You're too modest.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: Oh, yes, I hear from some friends that the Dukes' armies are very frequently on the move now. They've put every core city of their duchies under strict martial law.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: You've always been on top of the news... could you lend me a sly word, whether war seems imminent?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: The papers certainly forecast it, don't they? After all, the Dukes' fleets did trundle up to Londinium's walls some while ago.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: I'm not much concerned with the Sarkaz. I'm referring to between the Dukes... ahem, based on hearsay, that is. Just hearsay.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: There's been a lot of Originium fuel circulating into County Trent. The Marquess and the Duke of Caster have always been jolly with each other, but County Trent and the Iron Duke's duchy share a border...

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: My, my, Mr. Hall, all intercity fuel trade requires inspection and approval. I presume you have some very good friends in municipal management, no?

spans.text: My, my, Mr. Hall, all intercity fuel trade requires inspection and approval. I presume you have some
good friends in municipal management, no?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: Ha... haha, just for business purposes.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: Miss Harmonie, you might not follow the war too closely, but... you came in from another city, didn't you?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: You've been fortunate not to run into any hassle when you did, but I do ask you take care on the return journey.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: I hear it's hideous in the villages beyond the nomadic cities. There's rebel elements popping up now and then. Even a case of arson a few days ago.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: What sort of rebel elements are these to earn your attention?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: Attention is a strong word—similar things happen in spades anywhere the bumpkins live.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: It's that fire that's strange... hahah. This might not be true, so pretend I'm just telling you about some country tale.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: Eyewitnesses say that fire wasn't quite your ordinary one. It was ferocious as an explosion, but not a hint of Originium explosives was found where it happened. And the nightmarish effort it took to extinguish it...
Unusual fire.
All too likely to be a coincidence, but all too familiar of a description to her.
Could it be... Loughshinny?
Harmonie is stunned.
'The Brigadier's' warning has certainly roused some anxieties deep in her heart. Ever since that Rhodes Island ship had sailed into Victoria, she'd been absent any hold of information on Loughshinny.
Someone, without a doubt, had been helping Rhodes Island cover their tracks. Clearly, this pharmaceutical company was not as simple as she first assumed.
And on the same coin, a Loughshinny aboard Rhodes Island would be a Loughshinny immensely difficult for the rest of Victoria's powers to find.
So why... why would Loughshinny leave the ship?
Why would she surface somewhere so close to Eblana?
From behind Harmonie, there is a gaze.
Her every move has been closely watched since the second she stepped into the ballroom.
But it is this moment when the gaze truly focuses on her.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Merchant
steps.text: Miss Harmonie?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: I'm sorry... I was just thinking about the dance tonight. Say, what color earrings would I be best off wearing?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: ...Sir, I assume you've seen the relevant dossier, as well as all my reports.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: I suggest we commence operation immediately...

steps.name: Screened Woman's Voice
steps.text: Very well done, youngster. Have you tried the whiskey-filled chocolates out on the table?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: I hope you're well, Duke of Caster. I didn't expect you would grace this party, let alone be waiting here.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Who could miss such a grand soirée? Just listening to the chamber performance blows my cares away, even from behind my partition.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I do hope you're enjoying yourself too.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: I'm... still on duty. I can't be complacent.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Our every effort is made so that the masses can enjoy their serene lives.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Intelligence officers may be the lookouts, forced to keep a tense nerve even in times of peace, but you'll have your serenity one day.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Lest I forget. How's your health?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: My gratitude for your concern, Duke. It floors me that you note the infection of an average intelligence officer like myself.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Don't be nervous. You're not hiding anything. As I say, you've done very well.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: By way of a reward, would you like a promotion after your mission is over, or would you like to quit?
